# P4 — seam requests

## 1. Register the implementation service in `MtgEngine.Api/Program.cs`

`CardsImplementationController` takes `CardImplementationService`, which takes the
`ICardFilePool` already registered and the `cards/` directory the pool already reads. Add
these two lines beside the existing `ICardFilePool` registration (Program.cs, after the
`DeckGate` line):

```csharp
// The status endpoints read the same generated files the pool reads, but the whole file —
// scenarios, candidates, the last verification — which the gate has no business knowing.
builder.Services.AddSingleton(new CardImplementationOptions(
    Path.Combine(builder.Environment.ContentRootPath, "..", "cards")));
builder.Services.AddSingleton<CardImplementationService>();
```

Without them `/api/cards/{oracleId}/implementation`, `/api/cards/coverage` and
`/api/cards/{oracleId}/implementation/choose` return 500 on the missing dependency. The
service and its tests do not need the registration: the tests construct it directly over a
temporary directory.

## 2. `MtgEngine.Cards.Pipeline` cannot compute the engine hash

`VerifyStage` has to write `Verification.EngineHash`, and `EventLogSerializer.EngineHash()`
lives in `MtgEngine.Rules`, which the pipeline does not reference (its csproj references
`MtgEngine.Cards` and nothing else). Rather than add the reference from inside my own box, the
stage takes the hash as a constructor argument and the caller that built the runner passes
`EventLogSerializer.EngineHash()` in. That keeps the pipeline off the engine.

If the coordinator would rather the pipeline reference the engine directly — it will need to
anyway to construct a `ScenarioRunner` for `pipeline verify` — then add to
`MtgEngine.Cards.Pipeline/MtgEngine.Cards.Pipeline.csproj`:

```xml
<ProjectReference Include="..\MtgEngine.Rules\MtgEngine.Rules.csproj" />
```

and `VerifyStage`'s `engineHash` argument can default to `EventLogSerializer.EngineHash()`.
Either way the stage's decision is unchanged; this is only about who computes the string.

## 3. Note, not a request: the runner places the board with events

`ScenarioRunner` builds the game with `OpeningHandSize: 0` and empty decks, then places the
scenario's board with `ObjectCreated`/`LifeChanged`/`ManaChanged` events and sets the step with
`StepBegan`, rather than walking the turn structure to the requested step. Walking would untap
what the scenario tapped (CR 502.3) and draw from a library the scenario did not fill (CR
504.1), so a scenario could not state a position. Every placement is in the log, so a run still
replays. If a later wave wants the turn-based actions of the setup turn to have happened, that
is a `GameSetup` flag, not a change to the runner's shape.
